extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, applicants, and USPTO exam/processing staff (those preparing or prosecuting U.S. patent applications)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and requirements from the MPEP governing inventor oaths/declarations, correction/updating of inventorship and inventor names, and related procedural/formal requirements for U.S. patent (provisional and nonprovisional) filings and continuing applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor oath/declaration requirement (non-provisional)
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor, or each individual who is a joint inventor of a claimed invention, in an application for patent (other than a provisional application) must execute an oath or declaration directed to the application, except as provided for in pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.64.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When joint inventors execute separate oaths or declarations, each oath or declaration should make reference to the fact that the affiant is a joint inventor together with each of the other inventors indicating them by name (e.g., stating belief to be original, first, and joint inventor together with 'A' or 'A & B'). Forms PTO/SB/01 and PTO/SB/01A may be used for applications filed before September 16, 2012. See MPEP § 602.08 et seq. for details specific to required inventor bibliographic information and identification of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath/declaration must reference foreign applications when priority is claimed
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless included in an application data sheet, oaths and declarations must make reference to any foreign application for patent (or inventor’s certificate) for which priority is claimed and any foreign application filed prior to the filing date of an application on which priority is claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant must recite all foreign applications filed prior to the application on which priority is claimed, giving the foreign application number, name of country or office, and filing date of each foreign application to which priority is claimed. See MPEP § 602.03 for information pertaining to defective oaths or declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: New oath/declaration when adding inventor in continuation/divisional
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly executed oath or declaration must be filed in a continuation or divisional application naming an inventor not named in the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a copy of a prior oath is used in a continuation/divisional filed after assignment of an application number, include a cover letter identifying the continuation/divisional application number and noting that the submitted oath is a copy from a prior application to avoid mismatching. Label the copy with the continuation/divisional application number in case the cover letter is separated.

rubrics_metrics.name: New oath/declaration required for continuation-in-part (CIP)
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly executed oath or declaration must be filed in any continuation-in-part application, which application may name all, more, or fewer than all of the inventors named in the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because a CIP may include new matter, a new oath/declaration is required regardless of whether inventors differ from the prior application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify changes to power of attorney or correspondence address in continuations/divisionals
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the power of attorney or correspondence address was changed during the prosecution of the prior application, the change in power of attorney or correspondence address must be identified in the continuation or divisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not identified, the Office may not recognize in the continuation or divisional application the change of power of attorney or correspondence address that occurred during prosecution of the prior application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor bibliographic data, signatures, and application identification in oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor’s oath or declaration must include certain inventor bibliographic information, name the inventor or each joint inventor and, except as otherwise provided, be signed by each inventor, and identify the application to which it is directed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 602.08(a) for bibliographic information requirements, § 602.08(b) for signature requirements, and § 602.08(c) for identifying the application. Supplemental correction by an ADS (37 CFR 1.76) may cure some deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not amend wording of oath/declaration after signing; correct deficiencies properly
rubrics_metrics.description: The wording of an oath or declaration should not be amended, altered or changed in any manner after it has been signed. If the wording is not correct or if all required affirmations have not been made or if it has not been properly subscribed to, a new oath or declaration should be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some deficiencies can be corrected by a supplemental paper such as an application data sheet (see 37 CFR 1.76 and MPEP § 601.05). Example: if the notary's jurisdiction evidence is missing, a notary certificate establishing jurisdiction will correct the deficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-examiner review and notices for defective oaths/declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners are no longer required to review inventor’s oaths or declarations filed in non-reissue applications. Non-examiner staff will review oaths/declarations filed before allowance for compliance with 37 CFR 1.63 or 1.64 and may send an informational notice or, at or after allowance, a requirement to correct deficiencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an oath/declaration in compliance with 37 CFR 1.63 or 1.64 is not submitted by allowance, a notice requiring the oath or declaration may be sent with the Notice of Allowability; the required oath/declaration must be submitted no later than the date on which the issue fee is paid (35 U.S.C. 115(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of copy of prior oath/declaration in continuing applications (post-Sept 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, a continuing application may be filed with a copy of an oath or declaration or substitute statement from the prior nonprovisional application, provided that the oath or declaration is in compliance with 37 CFR 1.63 or the substitute statement complies with 37 CFR 1.64.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy submitted in a continuing application filed on or after September 16, 2012 must meet the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 115 and 37 CFR 1.63/1.64 as in effect for applications filed on or after that date. If the earlier-filed application was before September 16, 2012, a new oath/declaration may be needed to meet post-AIA requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship determination for continuing applications (post-Sept 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: For continuing applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, the inventorship is the inventor or joint inventors specified in the application data sheet (ADS) filed before or with the copy of the inventor’s oath or declaration from the earlier-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an ADS is not filed before or with the copy of the prior oath/declaration, the inventorship is the inventorship in the copy of the prior oath/declaration unless accompanied by a statement, signed by a 37 CFR 1.33(b) party, stating the name of each inventor in the continuing application. Any new joint inventor must execute an oath/declaration (or a substitute statement if permitted).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.48(a) requirements for correcting inventorship in nonprovisional application
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request to correct or change the inventorship once the inventorship has been established under §1.41 must include: (1) an application data sheet in accordance with §1.76 that identifies each inventor by his or her legal name; and (2) the processing fee set forth in §1.17(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ADS submitted with a request under 37 CFR 1.48(a) must identify the information being changed with underlining for insertions and strike-through or brackets for text removed. 37 CFR 1.48(a) permits correction for improper inventorship and where prosecution results in the need to add or delete inventors (e.g., claim changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.48(b): oath/declaration or substitute statement for added inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or declaration as required by §1.63, or a substitute statement in compliance with §1.64, will be required for any actual inventor who has not yet executed such an oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, the oath/declaration required must comply with 37 CFR 1.63 in effect for those applications. A substitute statement under 1.64 is only available for applications filed on or after that date. For applications filed before that date, pre-AIA 1.63 applies. See MPEP § 602.01(b) and § 604 for substitute statement requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.48(c): fee when request filed after Office action on the merits
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request to correct or change the inventorship under paragraph (a) filed after the Office action on the merits has been given or mailed in the application must also be accompanied by the fee set forth in §1.17(d), unless the request is accompanied by a statement that the request to correct or change the inventorship is due solely to the cancelation of claims in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The additional fee applies in addition to the ordinary processing fee set forth in §1.17(i) unless the change arises solely from claim cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.48(d): correction in provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a cover sheet as prescribed by §1.51(c)(1) is filed in a provisional application, any request to correct or change the inventorship must include: (1) a request, signed by a party set forth in §1.33(b), to correct the inventorship that identifies each inventor by his or her legal name; and (2) the processing fee set forth in §1.17(q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an inventor is being added in a provisional application, applicants should also file a corrected ADS or a new cover sheet providing the residence of all inventors. For provisional applications it may not be necessary to correct inventorship under 1.48(d) unless there would be no overlap of inventors upon filing the nonprovisional application with the correct inventorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.48(f): correcting/updating inventor name or order in nonprovisional
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request to correct or update the name of the inventor or a joint inventor, or the order of the names of joint inventors, in a nonprovisional application must include: (1) an application data sheet in accordance with §1.76 that identifies each inventor by his or her legal name in the desired order; and (2) the processing fee set forth in §1.17(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.48(f) permits changes for legal name changes (e.g., marriage), typographical/transliteration errors, or reversal of family/given names, and allows adjusting order of joint inventors (e.g., to control printed patent order). For some deficiencies/inaccuracies an applicant may submit a new inventor’s oath/declaration to correct earlier inaccuracies; some corrections may be made with an ADS (see MPEP § 601.05). Note that changing order in a provisional application is not provided for (provisionals do not become printed patents).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.48 does not apply to reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.48 does not apply to reissue applications as noted; where correcting inventorship in a patent via reissue, see 37 CFR 1.171-1.175 and MPEP § 1412.04. Where correcting via a certificate of correction, see 37 CFR 1.324 and MPEP § 1481. See 37 CFR 1.48(i) for correction of inventorship in interferences and contested cases before the PTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to correct inventorship for issues that are the subject of reissue or certificate of correction follow their own procedures and CFR provisions; do not use 1.48 for reissue corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship overlap requirement for benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 120 permits a continuing application to claim the benefit of the filing date of a copending previously filed parent application provided there is inventorship overlap between the continuing application and the parent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the inventive entity of a continuing application includes an inventor named in the parent application, the inventorship overlap required by 35 U.S.C. 120 is met. Refilling to change inventorship could result in loss of a benefit claim if there is no overlap in inventorship between the two applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition of inventor may affect power of attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: A correction of inventorship may result in the loss of power of attorney in applications filed on or after September 16, 2012: 37 CFR 1.32(e) provides that if the power of attorney was granted by the originally named inventive entity, and an added inventor pursuant to 37 CFR 1.48 does not provide a power of attorney consistent with the original, the addition results in loss of that power of attorney upon grant of the 37 CFR 1.48 request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision does not preclude a practitioner from acting in a representative capacity pursuant to 37 CFR 1.34, if applicable. Applicants should be aware of potential effects on representation when adding inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form PTO/AIA/40 available to request correction of inventorship/name/order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office has a form PTO/AIA/40 to request correction in a patent application (other than a reissue application) relating to inventorship, an inventor name, or order of names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/AIA/40 is reproduced in the MPEP and is available on www.uspto.gov. Use it to request corrections under 37 CFR 1.48 where appropriate. For oaths/declarations before Sept 16, 2012, forms PTO/SB/01 and PTO/SB/01A may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign-executed oaths: authentication and Hague apostille
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath executed in a foreign country must be properly authenticated. The Hague 'Apostille' Convention abolishes the requirement of diplomatic/legalization certificates for member countries; the Office will accept documents sworn to before a notary public in a member country if the document bears or has appended an apostille certifying the notary’s authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the oath is made in a foreign country not a member of the Hague Convention, the authority of the officer must be proved by certificate of a diplomatic or consular officer of the United States. Where the oath is taken before an officer whose authority is not authenticated or accompanied by an apostille, the application is accepted for examination but the applicant should submit a new oath properly authenticated, an apostille, or a declaration under 37 CFR 1.68. The Office does not return improperly authenticated oaths for proper authentication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-English oaths/declarations must be in language understood and include English translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever an individual making an oath or declaration cannot understand English, the oath or declaration must be in a language that such individual can understand and shall state that such individual understands the content of any documents to which the oath or declaration relates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless the foreign-language text is in a form provided by the PTO or in accordance with PCT Rule 4.17(iv), it must be accompanied by an English translation together with a statement that the translation is accurate. For an oath or declaration filed under §1.63 the translation may be filed in the Office no later than two months from the date applicant is notified to file the translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may require additional information for 1.48 requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may require such other information as may be deemed appropriate under the particular circumstances surrounding the correction of inventorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to provide additional documentation or statements as requested by the Office when submitting a 37 CFR 1.48 request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of 37 CFR 1.48 requests by OPAP (post-Sept 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for correction of inventorship under 37 CFR 1.48 filed on or after September 16, 2012 will be handled by the Office of Patent Application Processing (OPAP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPAP will process 1.48 requests; see MPEP references for procedure and replies. For requests filed before that date, see the earlier MPEP revision references noted in the text.
